posts.cooked:
I’m seeing what looks like the same issue on my Mac.

The Grokbot conversation appears to be stuck on the desktop app and will not refresh. The bot itself is still working normally in the cloud, and the same conversation is current and usable in the iOS app.

Desktop symptoms:

  • Existing Grokbot conversation shows “Couldn’t load conversation” / appears stuck
  • Clicking Retry does nothing
  • Messages sent from the desktop may show “failed to send,” but the bot can still receive them server-side
  • The desktop view does not update with the bot’s latest responses
  • Other Grokbot conversations may still load, so this does not appear to be a total connectivity failure

Troubleshooting already tried:

  • Force-quit and restarted the desktop app
  • Signed out and back in
  • Updated Grokbot’s Agent Computer
  • Switched the Mac from normal Wi-Fi to an iPhone hotspot
  • Retried the affected conversation multiple times

None of those changed the behavior.

Meanwhile:

  • Grokbot is still running and doing work in the cloud
  • iOS shows the current conversation correctly
  • Commands sent to the bot are still being received/executed
  • Only the macOS desktop conversation view seems stale / unable to reattach or refresh

This makes it look more like a desktop conversation/session synchronization or attachment issue than an Agent Computer or network problem.

Happy to provide logs or other diagnostics if the team wants anything specific checked.

posts.cooked: same issue here on 0.43. CoS stopped connecting in macos. iphone is fine. tried rebooting and reinstalling grokbot. no luck

Same 0.43.0 Mac bug as this thread. iOS on the same account and same Wi‑Fi is fine. The cloud bots are working.

After I updated the Mac app to 0.43.0 the conversation pane went stale (“showing saved messages / out of date”). Sidebar previews were already newer than the open thread. I fully quit, then signed out and back in. That cleared the cached thread and left “Couldn’t load conversation. Check your connection and try again.” Retry does nothing. It happens on every conversation I open, not just one.

The Mac app is not offline. Sidebar last-message previews update live when I send from the iPhone. The computer/monitor pane works; I can see the bot’s screen. Routines load. I can send from the Mac composer. A test message I sent from Mac appeared in the thread as my own bubble. The bot reply showed immediately in the Mac sidebar and on iOS, but it never appeared in the Mac transcript.

So on desktop, my own outgoing message can render. Old history and incoming bot replies do not. Everything else in the same window is alive.

Already tried: Retry, Cmd+Q and reopen, sign out and sign in, opening a different conversation, same network as the working iPhone. I have not used Reset, Recover, or Update Agent Computer, and I have not created a new bot or reinstalled.

I’ve now confirmed this is isolated to ONE specific Grokbot conversation/bot
(Cecil), not a general macOS Grok Bot failure on my account.

What I’m seeing:

  • Cecil’s conversation is still current and fully usable on iOS.
  • Cecil is fully operational in the cloud and continues doing work.
  • Commands sent from the Mac may show “failed to send”, but Cecil still
    receives and executes them server-side.
  • Cecil’s macOS conversation pane remains stale / cannot refresh.
  • Clicking Retry still does nothing.

Most importantly:

  • My OTHER Grokbot conversations/bots on the SAME Mac app load and update
    normally.
  • I can see messages/updates from those other bots on macOS.
  • Cecil can communicate with/update those other bots, and those updates are
    visible on the Mac.
  • So the Mac app itself is not generally offline, and the shared Agent

  • force quit/relaunch
  • sign out/sign in
  • repeated Retry
  • switched from normal Wi-Fi to iPhone hotspot
  • Updated Agent Computer

None changed Cecil’s desktop conversation.

This now looks much more like a stale/broken macOS attachment or synchronization
binding for this specific conversation/session, rather than a network issue or
Agent Computer failure.

cloud state?

I can provide any account/session/conversation identifiers or logs that would

posts.cooked:
MAJOR NEW REPRODUCTION / DIAGNOSTIC UPDATE

I attempted to migrate the affected bot (Cecil) to a fresh duplicate called
“Cecil v2” because the original Cecil macOS conversation remained broken.

Cecil v2 initially worked normally on macOS.

It successfully completed a long sequence of interactions, including:

  • reading durable handoff state
  • reconciling repo/orchestration state
  • inspecting its routines
  • reporting current worker/research status
  • inspecting its disabled managed-worker-exit-wake webhook routine

The conversation was completely functional throughout all of this.

Then I used Grokbot’s SECRET INPUT UI to securely enter/save the Webhook URL
for Cecil v2’s disabled managed-worker-exit-wake routine.

The UI showed:

“Cecil v2 exit-wake Webhook URL — Saved securely and kept private.”

Immediately after this secret-input operation, Cecil v2’s macOS conversation
began exhibiting the SAME failure mode as the original Cecil conversation:

  • messages show “Failed to send”
  • transcript/session no longer behaves normally on desktop
  • this occurred immediately after the webhook URL secret-input event

This is especially important because the webhook migration itself had NOT
occurred yet:

  • v2 webhook routine was still disabled
  • webhook key had not yet been supplied
  • shared runtime env had not been changed
  • no worker had been launched
  • no webhook smoke test had occurred

So this does NOT appear to be caused by my webhook code actually firing.

The apparent trigger is the Grokbot/macOS conversation handling around the
webhook SECRET INPUT / webhook credential workflow itself.

This is now a reproducible case:

  1. Create/duplicate healthy bot
  2. Bot conversation works normally on macOS
  3. Perform webhook secret-input operation
  4. macOS conversation immediately develops the same broken send/sync behavior

The original affected Cecil also owns webhook routines, which may now be
relevant to the original failure.

Please investigate the desktop conversation/session handling associated with
Grokbot webhook credentials / secret-input events.

I am preserving both affected bot instances and will not delete them so the
team can inspect their server-side state.
